children: shares edged 0.18% higher to $258.23 at 9:45 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, as Anthropic's IPO filing put at least $110 billion of committed Amazon compute spending on public view. Anthropic plans to price its offering on November 18 at $70 to $78 a share. Trading on Nasdaq under ANT is set to begin the next day.

The filing also shows at least $121.3 billion committed to Google from April 2026 to July 2033, plus $47.2 billion to $49.2 billion to Microsoft from November 2026 to June 2033. A Yahoo Finance analysis of the amended S-1 counted about $900.9 billion in total committed spending. These are minimum purchase obligations, not revenue Amazon has already booked.

Amazon's $110 billion floor is about 9% below Google's $121.3 billion, so on paper AWS is not Anthropic's largest compute supplier. A public listing also gives Amazon a market-priced customer whose ability to pay will partly track its own share price. GuruFocus gives Amazon a GF Score of 93/100, with strong profitability and momentum. Its GF Value of $259.58 sits about 0.5% above the share price, a fairly valued reading, so the Anthropic upside is not obviously cheap here. The next test is Wednesday's pricing and whether demand lands at the top of the range.

title: Amazon Stocks Edge Higher as Anthropic IPO Reveals $110 Billion Compute Pledge
